b2b_territory_optimization.allocator module

class b2b_territory_optimization.allocator.TerritoryAllocator(target_metric: str = 'Estimated_TAM', territory_prefix: str = 'Territory')[source]

Bases: object

Allocates accounts into k balanced territories within a specific Taxonomy Bucket. It uses a Greedy heuristic (LPT-inspired) to balance continuous metrics (like TAM) while respecting hard locks.

Methods

allocate_all_taxonomies(schema, ...[, ...])

Applies allocation across all buckets in a TaxonomySchema.

allocate_bucket(df_bucket, num_territories, ...)

Allocates a single bucket into num_territories.

allocate_by_capacity(schema, target_capacity)

Dynamically predicts required headcount per bucket based on capacity and allocates territories automatically.

predict_territory_count(df_bucket, ...)

Predicts the required number of territories (k) for a bucket based on a target capacity.
allocate_all_taxonomies(schema, num_territories_per_bucket: Dict[Tuple, int], locked_assignments: Dict[str, str] | None = None) → DataFrame[source]

Applies allocation across all buckets in a TaxonomySchema.

Parameters:

  • schema – An initialized TaxonomySchema object.

  • num_territories_per_bucket – Dict mapping Taxonomy Key -> number of territories.

allocate_bucket(df_bucket: DataFrame, num_territories: int, taxonomy_name: str, locked_assignments: Dict[str, str] | None = None) → DataFrame[source]

Allocates a single bucket into num_territories.

Parameters:

  • df_bucket – The accounts in this taxonomy bucket.

  • num_territories – How many territories to carve this bucket into.

  • taxonomy_name – String representation of the bucket (e.g., “AMER_Enterprise”).

  • locked_assignments – Dict mapping Account_ID -> target Territory_ID. These accounts will NOT be moved.

Returns:

DataFrame with a new column ‘Territory_ID’.

allocate_by_capacity(schema, target_capacity: float, locked_assignments: Dict[str, str] | None = None) → DataFrame[source]

Dynamically predicts required headcount per bucket based on capacity and allocates territories automatically.

Parameters:

  • schema – An initialized TaxonomySchema object.

  • target_capacity – The target capacity per territory (e.g., TAM quota per rep).

predict_territory_count(df_bucket: DataFrame, target_capacity: float) → int[source]

Predicts the required number of territories (k) for a bucket based on a target capacity.

Parameters:

  • df_bucket – The accounts in this taxonomy bucket.

  • target_capacity – The target value for the target_metric (e.g., $1,000,000 TAM).

Returns:

The predicted number of territories (minimum 1).

Return type:

int

b2b_territory_optimization.assignment module

class b2b_territory_optimization.assignment.SellerAssignmentMatrix(territories: List[str])[source]

Bases: object

Handles mapping different types of sellers (AEs, SEs, SDRs) to optimized territories. Supports 1:1, 1:N, and N:1 coverage models.

Methods

add_role(role_name, territories_per_seller)

Registers a seller role and its coverage model.

export_to_hierarchy([hierarchy_columns_order])

Exports the staffing roster into a flat hierarchy format designed explicitly to be ingested by b2b_revenue_forecasting.SalesHierarchy.

generate_assignments()

Generates the staffing matrix assigning hypothetical reps to territories based on the defined rules.

get_territory_roster()

Pivots the assignments so each row is a territory and columns are roles.
add_role(role_name: str, territories_per_seller: float)[source]

Registers a seller role and its coverage model.

Parameters:

  • role_name – e.g. “AE”, “SE”, “SDR”

  • territories_per_seller –

    • 1.0 means 1:1 (One seller covers exactly one territory)

    • 3.0 means 1:3 (One seller covers three territories)

    • 0.5 means 2:1 (Two sellers cover one territory)

export_to_hierarchy(hierarchy_columns_order: List[str] | None = None) → DataFrame[source]

Exports the staffing roster into a flat hierarchy format designed explicitly to be ingested by b2b_revenue_forecasting.SalesHierarchy.

Parameters:

hierarchy_columns_order – The desired top-down order of roles (e.g., [‘Regional_VP’, ‘Sales_Manager’, ‘Account_Executive’]). If None, uses the roles as they were added.

Returns:

A clean DataFrame ready for SalesHierarchy.from_dataframe(df, path_cols=…)

generate_assignments() → DataFrame[source]

Generates the staffing matrix assigning hypothetical reps to territories based on the defined rules.

get_territory_roster() → DataFrame[source]

Pivots the assignments so each row is a territory and columns are roles. If a territory has multiple sellers of the same role (N:1), their IDs are comma-separated.

b2b_territory_optimization.intelligent_assignment module

class b2b_territory_optimization.intelligent_assignment.IntelligentAssigner(sellers_df: DataFrame, allocated_df: DataFrame, taxonomy_columns: List[str])[source]

Bases: object

Uses Bipartite Matching (the Hungarian Algorithm) to mathematically assign real human sellers to optimized territories based on fit criteria and strict dimension matching.

Methods

assign_sellers()

Runs the Bipartite Matching Algorithm to optimally assign sellers.

build_cost_matrix()

Builds the cost matrix where rows are Sellers and columns are Territories.
assign_sellers() → DataFrame[source]

Runs the Bipartite Matching Algorithm to optimally assign sellers. Returns a DataFrame mapping Seller_ID to Territory_ID.

build_cost_matrix() → Tuple[ndarray, List[str], List[str]][source]

Builds the cost matrix where rows are Sellers and columns are Territories. :returns: Cost Matrix, List of Seller IDs, List of Territory IDs

b2b_territory_optimization.reassignment module

class b2b_territory_optimization.reassignment.ReassignmentEngine(allocated_df: DataFrame, target_metric: str = 'Estimated_TAM')[source]

Bases: object

Handles manual manager overrides (moving an account from one territory to another). Automatically calculates the resulting imbalance and suggests counter-moves to restore equilibrium.

Methods

get_imbalance([taxonomy_bucket])

Calculates the current total metric per territory.

move_account(account_id, new_territory_id)

Manually moves an account to a new territory.

suggest_rebalance(over_territory, ...[, ...])

Suggests accounts (or combinations of accounts) to move from the over-allocated territory to the under-allocated territory to minimize their difference.
get_imbalance(taxonomy_bucket: str | None = None) → DataFrame[source]

Calculates the current total metric per territory. If taxonomy_bucket is provided, limits analysis to territories starting with that string.

move_account(account_id: str, new_territory_id: str)[source]

Manually moves an account to a new territory.

suggest_rebalance(over_territory: str, under_territory: str, excluded_account_ids: List[str] | None = None, top_n: int = 5) → List[Dict][source]

Suggests accounts (or combinations of accounts) to move from the over-allocated territory to the under-allocated territory to minimize their difference.

Parameters:

  • over_territory – Territory to take accounts from.

  • under_territory – Territory to give accounts to.

  • excluded_account_ids – List of account IDs the manager refuses to move.

  • top_n – Number of suggestions to return.

b2b_territory_optimization.taxonomy module

class b2b_territory_optimization.taxonomy.TaxonomySchema(df: DataFrame, taxonomy_columns: List[str])[source]

Bases: object

Defines the strict hierarchical boundaries for territories. Accounts are grouped into “Taxonomy Buckets” based on the specified columns. Territory optimization happens strictly WITHIN these buckets, ensuring hard constraints (e.g. an SMB account cannot end up in an Enterprise territory).

Methods

get_all_bucket_keys()

Returns a list of all unique taxonomy combinations.

get_bucket(taxonomy_values)

Returns the accounts in a specific taxonomy bucket.

get_bucket_summary()

Returns a summary of account counts and total TAM per bucket.
get_all_bucket_keys() → List[Tuple][source]

Returns a list of all unique taxonomy combinations.

get_bucket(taxonomy_values: Tuple) → DataFrame[source]

Returns the accounts in a specific taxonomy bucket.

get_bucket_summary() → DataFrame[source]

Returns a summary of account counts and total TAM per bucket.
